Novaload's LOAD routine, in the tape buffer: the boot program points the KERNAL's LOAD vector ($0330) at it, and the game's block loader ($2A62-$2AD2) reaches it through the KERNAL's LOAD. A device other than 1 (tape) goes to the KERNAL's own load at $F4A5. It starts CIA 1's timer A at $81F4, maps all RAM with I/O ($01 = $05), waits for the lead-in of 0 bits and a 1, then reads $AA, the name's length (checked against $B7) and the name (checked against ($BB)), and starts again on any mismatch. The six header bytes go to $AC-$B1 (load address with the page one before the first, end address, bytes in the last page, page count); each page follows its running checksum. Status $30 in $90 on a checksum error, 0 when done; it then waits a moment, sets $01 = $37, returns the end address in X/Y and runs IOINIT ($FF84) keeping $DD00 (the video bank). The border flashes as bytes arrive ($03DE).
`jsr $F817`, the KERNAL's "press play on tape" wait; the game's block loader writes $AD here ($2A67-$2A69), turning it into a harmless `lda $F817`, so a load asks nothing on the bitmap screen.
Adds the byte read last ($AA) to the running checksum $A3, then reads the next byte (falls into novaload_get_byte).
Reads one byte from tape, lowest bit first: starts from $7F, a marker whose 0 bit falls out into the carry after the eighth bit; returns it in A and $AA.

Waits for the next pulse (CIA 1's FLAG, bit 4 of $DC0D), reads timer A's high byte and restarts the timer from $81F4 ($DC0E = $11): a pulse longer than 500 cycles leaves bit 7 clear and reads as 1. The bit is rotated into the byte on the stack; loops until the marker comes out. Flashes the border.
The last bytes of the tape buffer after the loader ($03FA a second RTS, then 00 FF FF 61 40); nothing in the game reads them.
Where the loader's last load returns ($40E2 jumps here after turning the screen on): jumps on to game_init at $04F7.

The computer's turn in an answer choice, every fourth frame (from $09AF). First it wanders: cpu_moves times it holds a random up or down (direction_bits) for 1-2 turns (cpu_wait). Moves the computer's cursor toward cpu_target: fire when there, else up ($2B87 = 1) when the cursor's slot number is above the target's, down (2) when below.
Counts cpu_wait down; when it runs out and moves remain (cpu_moves), picks a new wait of 1-2 turns and a random up or down.

Picks the computer's answer. Easy or Hard (display state 11): Hard (1) when the first team's score ($38A6) is ahead of the computer's ($38A7), else a random one of the two. Four answers: when the first team is ahead, the right answer's slot ($3506) with probability 192/256, else (and always when the computer is level or ahead) a random slot 0-3 other than the one the first team already chose ($2B91, $FF when none). Sets $2B84 so the decision is made once.
Stores the decision in cpu_target and marks it made ($2B84).
The answer slot the computer has decided on (written $095D, $097A; read $08EE, $08FC).
The computer's stick for answer_cursor_frame, active high (1 up, 2 down, $10 fire): written at $08D8, $090C, $0930, read at $08DB.

Display states 7 (four answers) and 11 (Easy or Hard), once a frame. Fire, once fire_held is clear, calls the effects code at $4FCB with X = 6 (when it is loaded, $33FE), copies the cursor to choice and sets step_done and fire_held. Until then each frame recolours the answers: the cursor's in the team's colour (team_colour $0CBE: red, blue); in the round where both teams answer ($1DC0 = 3) team 0's red, team 1's blue, purple where they meet. Then draws the colours (answer_bars_draw $0A77).
Ten bytes no code reaches, between `jmp cpu_answer_frame` and `jsr read_input`: they decode as `ldy $F9 / ldx $0CB8,Y / lda #0 / sta $0AF4,X`, which would clear the colour of the team's cursor.
The human team's turn: reads its stick (read_input).
Stores the stick and moves the team's cursor: down (bit 1 low) unless at answer_last, up (bit 0 low) unless at 0.

Skips the fire test once step_done is set.

Clears fire_held.
Sets the four answer colours (choice_colour): all 0, then the cursors' colours as answer_cursor_frame says.
One team's cursor in its colour (team_colour).
When both teams answer at once, handles team 0 after team 1 in the same frame.
